cards.text: The writer of Hebrews is writing to fellow believers, and he's just spent a whole chapter showing that Jesus is a priest forever (Hebrews 3:1; 7:17). Now he cuts straight to the point: we really do have a high priest like that. Friend, when somebody says 'here's the point,' that's when I stop sneaking cookie dough and LISTEN.

cards.question: The writer says we have a high priest like that. Where did He sit down?

answers.text: At the right hand of God's throne in heaven
Beside the altar in the temple courts
On Mount Sinai with the seventy elders

cards.text: He's seated, and He's STILL on the job: He ministers in the sanctuary, the true tabernacle. Meanwhile, I sit down for one second and three trays of cookies burn.

cards.question: True or false: The true tabernacle where Jesus ministers was set up by man.

cards.text: So what does a high priest actually DO all day? The writer lays out the job description, plain and simple.

cards.question: According to the writer, what is every high priest appointed to do?

answers.text: Guard the ark of the covenant

cards.text: So Jesus, as High Priest, had to have something to offer too. Now here's a twist: on earth, there are already priests who offer gifts according to the law.

cards.question: True or false: The writer says that if Jesus were on earth, He would still serve as a priest there.

cards.text: So what about the place where those earthly priests serve? The writer describes it by comparing it to what's in heaven.

cards.question: How does the writer describe the place where the earthly priests serve?

answers.text: A copy and shadow of what is in heaven
A gate that opens straight into heaven
A throne room filled with heaven's glory

cards.question: That's why Moses, Israel's leader, was warned when he was about to build the tabernacle. What did he have to follow?

answers.text: The pattern shown him on the mountain
The design King David gave Solomon
The measurements shown Ezekiel in a vision

cards.text: Now, however, Jesus has received a much more excellent ministry. A shadow is nice, but you can't eat the shadow of a cookie, and believe me, back in that dark drawer I TRIED.

cards.question: True or false: The writer says the covenant Jesus mediates is better and is founded on better promises.

cards.text: So why a new covenant at all? The writer reasons it out: if that first covenant had been without fault, nobody would have gone looking for a second one.

cards.question: The first covenant had a problem. The writer says God found fault with the ___.

cards.text: Then the writer quotes God's words, first spoken through the prophet Jeremiah (Jeremiah 31:31): "Behold, the days are coming, declares the Lord, when I will make a new covenant". When God says BEHOLD, friend, you put the phone DOWN.

cards.question: True or false: God says He will make this new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah.

cards.text: God says the new one won't be like the covenant He made with their fathers, back when He took them by the hand to lead them out of Egypt. By the HAND, friend, not a map and a 'good luck out there.'

cards.question: Why won't the new covenant be like the one God made when He led them out of Egypt?

answers.text: They did not keep His covenant
The priests grew too old to serve

cards.text: So what's different this time? Back at Sinai, God's words went on tablets of stone (Exodus 34:1), but this new covenant gets written in a whole new place.

cards.question: In the new covenant, God will put His laws in their minds and inscribe them on their ___.
Along with writing His laws on them, what else does God promise in this new covenant?

answers.text: He'll be their God and they'll be His people
He'll be their shield and they'll be His army
He'll be their guide and they'll be His travelers

cards.text: In this new covenant, God says, nobody will have to tell a neighbor or a brother to know the Lord. No more reminders, which would be rough on me, friend, because I remind bakers to check the oven every NINETY SECONDS.

cards.question: In the new covenant, why will no one need to tell a neighbor or brother to know the Lord?

answers.text: The priests will do all the teaching
The law will be read in every town

cards.text: Then God says, "For I will forgive their iniquities". Friend, if I could stamp one line on every cookie box in this bakery, THAT'S the one.

cards.question: God says He will forgive their iniquities and will remember their sins ___.

cards.text: The writer drives it home: by speaking of a new covenant, God has made the first one obsolete. And believe me, I know a thing or two about a shiny new stamper showing up on the counter.

cards.question: What does the writer say will happen to what is obsolete and aging?

answers.text: It will stand beside the new

findings.problem: The question says 'The writer says we have a high priest like that.' The phrase 'like that' points back to card 1, which is no longer on screen. The question never says what kind of high priest is meant.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The setup says the writer describes the earthly place 'by comparing it to what's in heaven.' Neither wrong answer on card 10 ('A gate that opens straight into heaven', 'A throne room filled with heaven's glory') is a comparison, so the setup rules them out. Only 'A copy and shadow' fits.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke 'you can't eat the shadow of a cookie, and believe me, back in that dark drawer I TRIED' doesn't hold together. There were no cookies in the drawer, and a dark drawer has no shadows. A stranger would say 'huh?'

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Verse 9 ends with God's response, 'and I disregarded them, declares the Lord.' No card tells this, and the card 6 answer covers only the people's failure. The baker leaves without an important detail of the verse.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The card says 'this new covenant gets written in a whole new place.' Hebrews 8:10 says God will put His laws in their minds and inscribe them on their hearts. It is the laws that are written, not the covenant.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card contrasts the stone tablets at Sinai (Exodus 34:1) with the new covenant being written 'in a whole new place.' Neither Hebrews 8 nor Exodus 34:1 states this contrast. The card adds a connection the texts don't make.

rule.text: Connecting passages. When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'He'll be their guide and they'll be His travelers' sounds forced and unnatural next to the familiar Bible wording of the right answer. This makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
